Making Best Friends... Better
Our board-certified veterinarians provide quality care and expertise in specialized surgery, cancer care and advanced imaging (CT) for your dog or cat. At OREV, your furry family member is our family, too.
Call Now
Advanced Surgery
Our veterinary surgery specialists are best suited to manage complex surgical cases in orthopedics, arthroscopy, soft tissue surgery, oncology surgery, trauma-related surgery and more.
More Details
Oncology Care
Our veterinary oncologist’s primary focus is to diagnose and treat various cancer conditions which may include utilizing surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation therapy and more.
More Details
Imaging/CT Services
Our in-house CT scan machine allows us to see beyond the surface to assess and create treatment plans for any concerns, including abdominal, thoracic conditions and underlying orthopedic issues.

Our board-certified veterinarians offer cutting-edge medical techniques in specialized surgery, oncology, and advanced imaging to address all of your pet’s medical needs.
We cherish the relationship between pet, owner, primary care veterinarian and specialist-veterinarian.
Our approach is a collaborative continuum that enhances and optimizes the pet’s well-being. Integrity, compassion, professionalism, and efficient communications are hallmarks of our specialty veterinary care.
Our great love for animals ensures the best specialty veterinary service possible.
Getting Started
Does My Pet Need a Referral?
Yes, our patients are referred by their primary care vet when their conditions indicate a need for specialized expertise in advanced surgery and oncology. When you contact us, we’ll review your pet’s health record and schedule an initial consultation to evaluate your pet’s needs.
Do I Need a Board-Certified Veterinarian?
If your pet requires specialized care outside the scope of your primary vet, you may need a board-certified veterinarian. Our board-certified vets have completed 3-4 years of additional training beyond veterinary school in specific areas of surgery and oncology.
What to Expect in the First Appointment?
During your initial appointment, one of our board-certified veterinarians will review your pet's history, perform a full examination, and follow-up with an in-depth discussion about your pet’s condition, ensuring  your questions are answered. Together, you and our specialist will discuss the possible treatment options and decide what is best for your pet and your family.
